system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Pathogenic IgG antibodies against the NR1 subunit of the NMDA receptor cause receptor internalization and reduced NMDA-receptor-mediated synaptic signaling; young women commonly develop prominent psychiatric symptoms followed by seizures, movement disorders, and autonomic instability, with an association with ovarian teratoma.
vignette: A 20-year-old woman develops anxiety, paranoia, and disorganized behavior several days after a flu-like illness. Over the next week she has a generalized seizure, repetitive orofacial dyskinesias, fluctuating consciousness, and episodes of tachycardia and labile blood pressure. Cerebrospinal fluid shows a mild lymphocytic pleocytosis. Pelvic ultrasonography shows an ovarian teratoma.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractor_notes: HSV encephalitis can cause fever, seizures, and behavioral changes, but the evolving psychiatric-hyperkinetic-autonomic syndrome in a young woman with an ovarian teratoma strongly favors anti-NMDAR encephalitis.
LGI1 encephalitis more often affects older adults and is classically associated with faciobrachial dystonic seizures and hyponatremia rather than the teratoma-associated anti-NMDAR syndrome.
A primary psychotic disorder does not explain the subsequent seizures, dyskinesias, fluctuating consciousness, autonomic instability, inflammatory CSF, and ovarian teratoma association.

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome requires dopamine-antagonist exposure and is characterized by severe rigidity, hyperthermia, and autonomic dysfunction rather than this progressive autoimmune encephalitic syndrome.
key_expl: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis commonly begins with psychiatric or behavioral symptoms and progresses to seizures, movement disorders, impaired consciousness, and autonomic instability. Young women have a well-established association with ovarian teratoma. Pathogenic IgG binds the NR1 subunit and causes NMDA-receptor internalization.
objective: Recognize anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis from the characteristic psychiatric, seizure, movement-disorder, and autonomic syndrome, particularly in a young woman with ovarian teratoma.
